$comment: Which code governs where, and how much of it codraft can check. A country listed here is NOT a claim that its code is encoded -- read rule_packs and confidence. Nothing in this file is legal advice, and no entry substitutes for the authority having jurisdiction.

icc.description: International Building Code and International Residential Code, as adopted and amended locally.
icc.note: The IBC is a model code with no force of its own. A state, emirate or municipality adopts an edition and amends it, so the adopted edition and its local amendments always govern.

icc-derived.description: A national code built on an IBC edition, with local amendments for climate, seismicity and practice.
codes: National code derived from the IBC
icc-derived.note: Checks run against the IBC provisions the national code was built from. Local amendments are not encoded and can be stricter; confirm each finding against the national document.

eurocode.description: EN Eurocodes for structural design, with fire, egress and energy set by national building regulations.
codes: National building regulations and national annexes
eurocode.note: The Eurocodes cover structural design, not room sizes or egress geometry. Those sit in each country's own building regulations and its National Annex, which are not encoded here. Only the practice baseline is applied.

uk.description: The Building Regulations for England, with Approved Documents giving practical guidance.
codes: Approved Documents B, K, M and others
uk.note: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own, divergent regulations. Resolve to the nation, not to 'UK'.

pk.family: Building Code of Pakistan and provincial by-laws
pk.description: A national code for structural and fire provisions, with planning controls set by each city's development authority.
codes: Building Code of Pakistan (Fire Safety Provisions) 2016
pk.authority: Pakistan Engineering Council; provincial development authorities (CDA, LDA, RDA, SBCA, PDA)
pk.note: Setbacks, coverage and height are fixed by the development authority for each city and vary by plot size and scheme. The encoded values are common by-law figures and must be confirmed against the authority for the specific scheme.

in.description: NBC 2016, adopted through state and municipal building by-laws.
in.authority: State urban development departments and municipal corporations
in.note: The NBC is a model code. States and municipalities adopt it with amendments, and the local development control rules govern setbacks, ground coverage and FAR/FSI.

ca.description: The NBC, adopted with amendments by each province.
ca.note: No NBC rule pack is encoded yet. Ontario, Quebec, BC and Alberta each publish their own code, which governs.

cn.description: Mandatory GB standards for design, fire and residential buildings.
codes: GB 50352 Uniform standard for design of civil buildings
GB 50016 Code for fire protection design of buildings
GB 50096 Design code for residential buildings
cn.note: No GB rule pack is encoded. The GB standards are mandatory and published in Chinese; a translation is not authoritative.

jp.description: The Building Standards Act and its Enforcement Order.
jp.note: No rule pack encoded. Setbacks and bulk are governed by the city planning system, including sunlight and setback slope controls with no equivalent in other codes.

national.description: A national code administered by a central ministry or standards body.
national.note: The national code for this country is not encoded, so only the practice baseline is applied. Its provisions govern and must be checked directly.

unknown.description: codraft has no mapping for which code governs here.
unknown.note: No code has been mapped for this country. Nothing in the report should be read as a statement about local law. Identify the authority having jurisdiction before relying on any of it.

au.description: The NCC, adopted by each state and territory.
au.note: No NCC rule pack is encoded yet, so only the practice baseline is applied. The NCC is free to read at the link.
